# Onboarding for handover-sandbox stopped at 30_secrets

**Repo:** agent-bureau

Onboarding `handover-sandbox` from `config/onboarding/handover-sandbox.json` stopped at step `30_secrets`, which was failed: GitHub GET /repos/dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/contents/.github/workflows/plan.yml?ref=stable answered 403, read as agent-bureau-bot on dreadnought-foundry — GitHub said "API rate limit exceeded for installation ID 123249480. If you reach out to GitHub Support for help, please include the request ID 9548:3A61E:7471AF7:A629088:6AE7E776 and timestamp 2026-11-02 01:29:27 " — GitHub rate-limited the read and asked for a wait of 1173 seconds, over the 15-minute cap $ONBOARD_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_MINUTES sets, so it was not taken; nothing is wrong, and re-running onboarding is the fix

Run: https://github.com/dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau/actions/runs/41372594855

## Log

- `onboarding: handover-sandbox 05_resume skip — no BUREAU_PAUSE_RECORD on dreadnought-foundry/handover-sandbox — it was not paused`
- `onboarding: handover-sandbox 10_makefile ok — dreadnought-foundry/handover-sandbox's Makefile on main carries real lint, typecheck, test and build targets`
- `onboarding: handover-sandbox 15_company skip — handover-sandbox's declaration takes its repo from the scaffold, not Slipway, so there is no company to create`
- `onboarding: handover-sandbox 20_repo skip — dreadnought-foundry/handover-sandbox carries the scaffold (.github/workflows/agent-task.yml on main) and CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE=subscription`
- `onboarding: handover-sandbox 25_aws_account skip — handover-sandbox's declaration names no aws_account, so there is no AWS account to make or bootstrap`
- `onboarding: handover-sandbox 30_secrets failed — GitHub GET /repos/dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/contents/.github/workflows/plan.yml?ref=stable answered 403, read as agent-bureau-bot on dreadnought-foundry — GitHub said "API rate limit exceeded for installation ID 123249480. If you reach out to GitHub Support for help, please include the request ID 9548:3A61E:7471AF7:A629088:6AE7E776 and timestamp 2026-11-02 01:29:27 " — GitHub rate-limited the read and asked for a wait of 1173 seconds, over the 15-minute cap $ONBOARD_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_MINUTES sets, so it was not taken; nothing is wrong, and re-running onboarding is the fix`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Re-running onboarding for handover-sandbox ends with outcome verified

🧩 planning-shape: **one-off** — One card, one pull request. It owes no plan artifact and stops for no green light.

**Why:** A transient GitHub rate limit stopped this one onboarding run, and the card's only deliverable is re-running onboarding for one repo until it ends verified, which is a single piece of work with no parts that depend on each other. — size tests checked: 1 contracts between the pieces, 2 two languages or two tiers, 3 a criterion counting something never enumerated, 4 an unbounded quantifier, 5 specific is not small, 6 cut on file footprint, not only on concern

**Stamped by:** `planner` · **model:** `claude-opus-5-5`

**Where it goes:** Queued. **Who handles it there:** reconcile.py.
🧠 model-attempt: claude-opus-5-5 (asked) / claude-opus-5-5 (answered) · cost $0.1045 — planning classifier read the card.

🔁 **Pre-approval critic — before this is built** — sent back — round 1 of 2. Every finding here is a defect in the card an agent can fix, so the planner revises the card in place and the critic reads it again.

Reason: This card asks for onboarding to be run again, which is an operator action and not a pull request, so an unattended builder has nothing to build and no way to meet the one criterion.

Every finding this round (6), ranked — the revision answers all of them, and the next round checks those fixes rather than finding these again:

1. This card asks for onboarding to be run again, which is an operator action and not a pull request, so an unattended builder has nothing to build and no way to meet the one criterion.
2. The only deliverable is "re-run onboarding until it ends verified". That changes no files, so there is no pull request for the build agent to open, and the card is stamped as buildable work (one-off) when it is really a hand step.
3. The criterion ("ends with outcome verified") can only be met by someone starting the onboarding run and watching it finish against live GitHub. A build agent cannot show that from a pull request, and the card names no file, change or test to point at.
4. The same failure has now happened on two separate runs about four minutes apart (the second run's wait was 1173 seconds, the first 1392). GitHub is still throttling the bot's installation, so an immediate re-run is likely to fail the same way. The card says "nothing is wrong", but it gives no wait …
5. If the planner wants this to be buildable work instead, the card needs to name a real code change (for example, letting the onboarding step wait longer or retry after a long rate-limit wait). Whether to change that 15-minute cap is a choice the card does not make, and I am not making it here.
6. The card body and the pipeline's own first comment quote two different run links and two different GitHub request ids. Either the card was refiled after a second failure or the text was merged from two runs. It should say which run it is about.

This card is not going to the build queue yet, and nothing here is for the CEO — it stays in Planning while the planner rewrites it to answer every finding above, and the critic reads it again.

plan-critic: stage=one-off round=1 result=SEND_BACK collisions=0 run=41372465328 — This card asks for onboarding to be run again, which is an operator action and not a pull request, so an unattended builder has nothing to build and no way to meet the one criterion.

🔁 The planner revised this card in place to answer the critic. What it changed, finding by finding:

Planner revision, round 1. One line per finding, in the critic's order.

1. **Operator action, not a pull request:** I rewrote the card as a code change. Onboarding's rate-limit cap goes from 15 to 60 minutes (`RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_DEFAULT` in `scripts/onboarding.py`), so a GitHub primary rate limit always ends in a wait and never in a stop and a card for a person. The re-run is no longer the deliverable.
2. **Changes no files:** the card now has a **Files:** line (`scripts/onboarding.py`, `scripts/test_onboarding.py`, `docs/customer-onboarding-runbook.md`, and a comment only in `.github/workflows/onboard.yml`) and a numbered change list, so the build agent opens one pull request. The one-off stamp now fits.
3. **Criterion needs live GitHub:** I removed "re-running onboarding ends verified" from the acceptance criteria. Every criterion now reads from the diff or the tests, including a new `TestRateLimitRetry` case that replays this card's own 1392-second wait and asserts it is slept and the next answer is returned.
   **Cut, for a person:** the re-run of `handover-sandbox` is cut from this card. Start it any time after 2026-11-01 17:49 PT, either by dispatching it or by waiting for the next push run that touches `config/onboarding/`, which still has it in range. Nobody needs to file a card for it.
4. **Re-run too soon, no wait given:** the card now gives the wait. Both stops count down to the same moment, 2026-11-01 17:49 PT, when the installation's hourly budget reset (17:25 PT + 1392 s = 17:29 PT + 1173 s). That is why the second run, started before it, failed the same way. It also explains the fix: the engine refused a 20–23 minute wait only because of the 15-minute cap.
5. **The cap is a choice the card does not make:** the card makes it now. The cap becomes 60, because GitHub's primary limit is an hourly window, so `X-RateLimit-Reset` is never more than an hour away. I checked this is an engineering setting and not a business choice. `onboard.yml` passes no `ONBOARD_*_WAIT_MINUTES` to the engine, so in CI the cap was always the default. The apply job already waits up to 180 minutes for routing inside its 360-minute timeout. `RATE_LIMIT_TRIES` stays 3, so one call waits at most twice. The card states the bound it accepts (every wait at its maximum in one run could pass 360), and the `onboard.yml` timeout comment will name the new wait.
6. **Two run links, two request ids:** the card now names both runs in a table: run, who started it, when it stopped (PT), wait and request id. It says it is about both. Run 41361158200 was the push run for PR #4476 and filed the card. Run 41372594855 was a dispatch of handover-sandbox two minutes later, found the card open by title and posted its stop as the first comment, which is what `onboard.yml`'s card step does by design. I kept the original log and labelled which run it came from.

🔁 The critic reads the revised card again on the next planning run, which has been started — nothing here is for the CEO. If the revision still does not satisfy it, the card parks in Triage for the operator with every finding named.

⚠️ **Pre-approval critic — before this is built** — the critic produced no result, and on this route that is not a pass — nothing else reads this card before it is built, so the critic reads it once more before a person is asked anything

This card is not going to the build queue yet, and nothing here is for the CEO yet — it stays in Planning, and the critic reads this card again on a fresh planning run, which has been started. If that read decides nothing too, the card goes to the CEO.
